newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Prince sees more British investment in Zimbabwe.
newsitem.headline: Prince sees more British investment in Zimbabwe.

text.p: Britain's Prince Andrew urged British businesses on Thursday to explore more investment and trade opportunities in Zimbabwe, saying its economic climate was improving rapidly.
The prince arrived in Zimbabwe on Tuesday for a three-day official visit during which he will witness a landmark joint military exercise by eight southern African nations.

Speaking at a business luncheon, he said Zimbabwe's recent economic reforms and liberalisation programme had opened up opportunitites for foreign companies to boost trade and their investment portfolios.
Britain is currently the largest foreign investor in Zimbabwe with over 300 companies and subsidiaries in its former colony.
"It is our desire that more British companies play a role in Zimbabwe's impressive economic development," he said.
"All that I have read and heard about Zimbabwe's impressive development suggests to me that a rapidly liberalising business sector has been a key element in that development," he said.

Prince Andrew is due to meet Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe on Wednesday before travelling to the southern African state's eastern Nyanga district where the 20-day regional military exercise is being staged.
Britain is partly funding the exercise which ends on April 20.

Some 1,100 troops from Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania and Zimbabwe -- all Commonwealth members -- are taking part in the exercise, the first of its kind in Africa aimed at honing peacekeeping skills.

London's Zimbabwe-based British Military Advisory and Training Team is helping run the exercise, code-named Blue Hungwe (Fish Eagle), which it says shows its "commitment to the development of regional peacekeeping operations in Africa".
President Mugabe will also witness the exercise on Thursday, which is based on United Nations tactics and techniques of international peacekeeping.
